It is completely understandable that you are worried about your mother, especially with a family history of dementia. Alongside missing appointments and misplacing things, other signs to watch for include difficulty completing familiar daily tasks, sudden changes in mood or personality, confusion about time or place, and struggling to follow conversations. 

When talking to her, try to approach the conversation with gentle support rather than confrontation. Since she brushes these off as senior moments, it can help to frame a doctor's visit as a routine wellness check rather than a dementia screening. You might mention that you want to rule out other easily treatable causes for memory slips, such as vitamin deficiencies or medication side effects. Using "I" statements, like "I love you and want to make sure we are staying on top of your health," can help her feel cared for instead of defensive. Offering to accompany her to a general checkup might be a comforting first step.
